newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu and Arafat speak by phone.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu and Arafat speak by phone.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a "message of peace" in a telephone conversation with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Sunday after defending government benefits for Jewish settlers.

Prior to the call, Netanyahu dispatched a personal envoy to Arafat in an apparent bid to ease tensions that have flared since the cabinet agreed on Friday to grant benefits such as tax breaks to settlers in the occupied West Bank.

The Palestinian Information Ministry had called the Israeli move, which could entice more Jews to join the 130,000 already living amid some two million Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza Strip, a declaration of war.
Asked by Israel's Itim news agency what he relayed to Arafat, Netanyahu replied: "A message of peace." A spokesman for Netanyahu confirmed the call and said he would give details later.
Netanyahu's envoy Yitzhak Molcho held talks with Arafat in self-ruled Gaza, the first such high-level contact in weeks between Israel and the PLO, a spokesman for the Palestinian president said.

Earlier, Netanyahu appeared on Israeli television and radio stations in a media offensive to defend the decision to grant benefits frozen by the previous Labour-led government he defeated in elections last May.
